references.text: Deuteronomy gives parallel laws about the release of Hebrew slaves after six years of service, with further details on how they should be treated upon their release.
Leviticus contains laws regarding the treatment of Israelite slaves in connection with the Jubilee year, which supplement the rules in Exodus 21:2.
Jeremiah condemns the people for breaking the covenant to release Hebrew slaves after six years, and refers to the law in Exodus 21:2.
The principle of the seventh year as a year of release also applies to debts, showing the broader connection between the Sabbath year and freedom.
The Sabbath year for the land follows the same seven-year cycle as the release of slaves, demonstrating God's principle of rest and freedom.
The Jubilee year proclaims liberty for all inhabitants of the land, which is an extension of the principle of release in the seventh year.
A direct legislative parallel that expands the rule of release to also include women.
A prophetic allusion that uses the law's rule of release as a basis to condemn the people's disobedience.
A theological justification for liberation that elaborates on the ethical and economic dimension of the law.
